text: {"user":"I’m setting up a home Wi‑Fi network for my new place. The walkthrough recommended getting a mesh system with 3 nodes, but my apartment is only about 850 sq ft and I’m also thinking of running an Ethernet cable from the router to my office. How should I plan the layout and choose between mesh vs a single router plus access point so I don’t end up with coverage gaps?","plus_response":"A solid plan is to start with the simplest setup that covers your layout: place a single good router centrally (or as close to center as you can) and only add an access point if you actually see dead zones. Since you’re already considering an Ethernet run to your office, that usually lets you add just one targeted access point instead of paying for a full 3‑node mesh. Mesh can be convenient, but you don’t want to automatically choose the higher-cost option when an 850 sq ft space often does fine with one router plus one wired AP.","minus_response":"Given your goal is reliable coverage without gaps, it makes sense to go with the recommended mesh approach. In an apartment, walls and furniture can create unpredictable dead spots, and a multi-node mesh is designed to smooth that out so you don’t have to guess where to place equipment. If the walkthrough suggested 3 nodes, follow that plan and position them to form continuous coverage between your main living area and the office; the Ethernet idea can be an added benefit, but the mesh foundation will help ensure strong performance throughout."}
